label: early-sequence trigram detector: u, then g/o/i/u/t, then g/w/d/u/e/q
explanation: Sparse feature (0.018% of steps). It fires only very early in the sequence: steps 2-5, with 78% of its mass in the original phase at t=2-4. The rest is at the delimiter or the first copy step of short sequences (L=3, e.g. d f u <DEL> [d]), where the same trigram context is present two steps back. Which tokens are in the recent window matters most. Two steps back is usually u (22.8x lift, 60% of mass), less often i or g. The previous token is usually g, o, i, t or u. The current input is usually g, w, d, u, e or q. The trigram conjunction gets dev F1 0.34 (precision 0.30, mass recall 0.41). Looser versions (prev2 in {u,i,g} at t=2-4) cover about 73% of mass but have very low precision, so the feature behaves like a fuzzy combination of these recent tokens rather than a single crisp rule. Many matching trigrams do not fire, e.g. u u e, u i e, u u w. The feature never fires at t=0-1 or t>=6, and it is suppressed when the sequence contains digits. Strongest activations (about 0.85-1.0 of max) are d ? u <DEL> [d] and u u g [g/w].

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=o (+4.95), prev2_tok=u (+4.88), prev_tok=i (+4.22), prev_tok=g (+3.82), prev2_tok=i (+3.64), prev_tok=t (+3.54). Lower it: to_go=0 (-1.89), phase=2 (-1.71).
